commentPreTextItems.html: 5.03pm Nandre Burger has the new ball straightaway. We are running three minutes behind schedule already. Yashasvi Jaiswal on strike. One wide slip in place
4.55pm All set for what promises to be an entertaining evening of cricket. The national anthems are on as we speak.
Kamal: "and we have Maharaja Burger as well in Indian McDonalds.. :p"
4.45pm Mustafa Moudi: "Since Maharaj (Hindi Word) means KING in English. Burger King are the Changes SA made tonight for this match :P"
Sasi Gowniwari: "Nobody can beat Ajju Bhai when it comes to winning the toss."

4.30pm South Africa have won the toss again, and it is no surprise that they have inserted India. Chasing is the way to go, Aiden Markram says. Left-arm quick Nandre Burger gets his debut. Keshav Maharaj and Donovan Ferreirs come in too. The players missing out are Marco Jansen and Gerald Coetzee, who are off to prepare for the Tests, and Tristan Stubbs.
Suryakumar Yadav says he would have batted first anyway. No changes for India.
Nikhil Kelkar: "I think of all Indian captains in recent memory, Surya seems to have the worst luck with the toss"
Sudhanshu: "With SKY as captain, perhaps they can get away from not doing the toss at all, he just looses it all the time"

4.20pm Bone dry, says Pommie Mbangwa about the pitch. Nice even grass. One side of the field is bigger than the other by 10m. Expect a lot of runs, he says. And as Pommie did his match report, Arshdeep Singh marked his run-up.

Shark: "Remember India's first ever T20I match played at Johannesburg over 17 years ago (2006) against Graeme Smith's South Africa. India was captained by Sehwag in a world before IPL and before MSD, the captain . Funnily enough I remember India winning that match, thanks to a 21 year old DK, who was the Man of the match then. Quite surreal that he is still technically an active T20I player now (and only one apart from MSD to play competitive cricket) and played the T20I WC as recently as 2022!"
4.15pm What to expect from the conditions in the Highveld? We await a pitch report but the last T20I here yielded 433 runs. This really is an ideal place to hit sixes.

4pm As thew Jo'burg afternoon gives way to evening, we welcome you to the decider of this T20I series after the first match was washed out and the second was won by South Africa. The weather forecast seems fine, and this should be a cracker in the rarefied air of the Highveld. Get your seat belts. Toss is in half an hour.

dismissalText.commentary: David Miller b Kuldeep Yadav 35 (25b 2x4 2x6 41m) SR: 140

commentTextItems.html: Kuldeep has the five-for on his birthday. Miller knows there is no point batting this innings out. He tries to hit out, shuffles across for the big sweep, and Kuldeep fires this in full and straight to hit the leg stump

commentPostTextItems.html: 8.35pm That brings us to an end for tonight. Entertaining short little series. Shame about the rain in the first match or we might have had a result. Now the captains share the spoils, and move on to the ODIs starting Sunday, which will be the Pink Day. Join us then, and thanks for tuning in tonight. Stay hydrated, and don't take mid-match assessments too seriously.

8.30pm Suryakumar Yadav, the winning captain, is also the Player of the match. He is hobbling around after his injury. He is also the Player of the Series. He says, and this is not verbatim: "I am good. I am able to walk so it is not that serious. It was wonderful scoring a hundred, and especially when it comes in a winning cause. One box we wanted to tick was play fearless brand of cricket. Really happy the boys showed a lot of character. Kuldeep is never happy with a three-for or a four-for. A perfect self birthday present."
"At mid innings break, a statement was indeed made: at this stage, I dare say that this might not be par!" Kaushik, it says "might". And it never says "below par"

8.27pm Aiden Markram says, and this is not verbatim: "To be honest, I wasn't toon unhappy with the 200 looking at how the pitch played as I watched it when fielding. It felt like a little stoppy and a little down when we were batting, while when we were fielding it looked like they could hit it anywhere."

8.17pm Big win to level the series after the first one was washed out and the second lost to South Africa. It looked like a par total for Johannesburg, but India managed to find movement of all three kinds: Siraj swung it in the air, the ball nipped when bowled on wobble seam, and then it turned and gripped and bounced indifferently when the spinners came on. The bowlers were too good to waste those conditions. Siraj playing around with Hendricks at the top of the innings will be a memorable spell of play in T20 cricket.

In the first innings of the match, Suryakumar Yadav recovered from a slow start to score a fourth T20I century full of the usual scarcely believable shots. He rolled over his ankle when fielding, and Jadeja led the team for the majority of the defence. Not only did all the bowling changes and field placements work, Jadeja himself took the big wicket of Markram and had figures of 3-0-25-2 to go with the five-for for Kuldeep.
Debs: "Kuldeep's last 6 balls read 1-0-1-4. Amazing"
Karthik Iyappan: "South Africa lost to SURYAKUMAR YADAV(100runs today) by 5 runs!!!

"@Sid - you are saying it looked like a par total. But mid innings break it was like below par. We can see how statements change after a result." Ashish, I await evidence to suggest I said the total was below par
